title: Compiler pipeline correctness as a transitivity chain of six per-pass simulations
intent: Prove the correctness of the whole bedrock2 compilation pipeline (six passes) by composing the six per-pass `phase_correct` lemmas with the transitivity lemma `compose_phases_correct`, so the top-level proof is nothing but the children applied in the order of `composed_compile`.

parent.name: composed_compiler_correct
parent.statement: phase_correct SrcLang (RiscvLang p_funcs stack_pastend ret_addr) composed_compile

children.name: compose_phases_correct
children.statement: phase_correct L1 L2 compile12 -> phase_correct L2 L3 compile23 -> phase_correct L1 L3 (compose_phases compile12 compile23)
children.closed_by: split; intros; fwd; eauto — destructs both phase_correct records [V12 C12] [V23 C23], then chains the two simulations with `eapply C12 in H1; eapply C23 in H1`, closing the metric obligation by `post_ext` and `eauto 10 with metric_arith`

applicability.goal_shape: A goal `phase_correct L_first L_last composed` where `composed` is a right-nested `compose_phases p1 (compose_phases p2 ... pn)` and `phase_correct` is a two-field simulation record (validity preservation plus a relational postcondition carrying a metric inequality).
applicability.use_when: each pass already has a `phase_correct` lemma of the same shape; the passes are composed in one fixed order (a `composed_compile` definition); a transitivity lemma `compose_phases_correct` is available.
applicability.avoid_when: a pass has no standalone `phase_correct` lemma yet (the chain forces one lemma per pass before the glue can be written); the composition order must be reordered or a pass reused; the intermediate languages must be written out explicitly so consecutive transitivity instances typecheck.

claims.claim: The parent `composed_compiler_correct` closes with `unfold composed_compile` and a single `exact` of a nested `compose_phases_correct` application over the six per-pass lemmas, in 9 proof lines (lines 635-643), with no other tactic.

Pipeline.v is built by the project's CI: `.github/workflows/debian.yml` runs `make` on pushes to `master`, and `compiler/Makefile`'s `noex` target compiles every `*.v` under `src/compiler` (which includes Pipeline.v).

The glue applies 7 direct lemmas (6 per-pass lemmas plus the transitivity lemma `compose_phases_correct`) in 9 lines; the longest project-lemma chain below the parent is 2 (`composed_compiler_correct` -> `flattening_correct` -> `flatten_functions_NoDup`); the six pass lemmas have 50, 34, 48, 46, 32, 20 proof lines respectively.
claims.evidence: parent lines 634-643; flattening_correct lines 274-324; flatten_functions_NoDup lines 249-260 (used at line 280); proof-line counts of the six pass lemmas at lines 274-324, 342-376, 391-439, 457-503, 552-584, 602-622

claims.claim: The authors deliberately separate the compositional core from the user-facing restatement: `compiler_correct` (line 682) is introduced with the comment 'restate composed_compiler_correct by unfolding definitions used to compose phases' (line 681), so the transitivity chain is the canonical statement and the restatement just unfolds it.

The one compositional lemma is reused rather than re-proved: `compiler_correct` consumes it at line 733 (`pose proof (phase_preserves_post (composed_compiler_correct p_funcs stack_hi ret_addr))`), and `compiler_correct_wp` in turn consumes `compiler_correct` at line 806.

metrics.how_counted: parent proof lines = 635-643 of Pipeline.v; child proof lines = the seven child site ranges summed (121-135, 275-324, 343-376, 392-439, 458-503, 553-584, 603-622); children_closed_by_automation counts how many of the six per-pass lemmas close with a single automated tactic (none does — each ends in a bespoke *_correct_aux / checker_correct / spill_fun_correct / flat_to_riscv_correct lemma).

consequences: Turns one large end-to-end simulation goal into one transitivity lemma plus n per-pass `phase_correct` lemmas, so each hole is one whole compiler pass — the natural unit for a bounded prover. Obligations: each child must be a full `phase_correct` record (both fields); the glue's application order must match `composed_compile`; the intermediate languages must be named so consecutive `compose_phases_correct` instances typecheck. Failure mode: the glue does no work itself, so a missing or misshaped per-pass lemma surfaces as a type error at the `exact`; if two passes share a language the intermediate must still be written out.
